sections.h2: Who sets and who collects property tax in Bourbon County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Two offices in the Paris courthouse building split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) in Room 15 sets the value. The Sheriff's Office in Room 104 sends the bills and takes the money.

The county directory lists the PVA at (859) 987-2152, extension 217, and the sheriff at (859) 987-2130. Each office keeps weekday hours from half past eight to four-thirty. The sheriff's page adds that the office shuts on holidays such as Good Friday, Memorial Day, Veterans Day and Thanksgiving.

sections.h2: How big is Bourbon County, and what does that mean for assessments?
sections.html:
Bourbon County covers roughly 290 square miles of mostly open, rolling farmland around Paris, with Millersburg and North Middletown as the smaller towns. Census figures put the population at 20,243 in 2025 and the housing stock at 9,399 units.

Home values here run well above neighboring Boyd County's $130,700 median. The Census Bureau's five-year survey values the typical owner-occupied home at $229,300, and owners live in 63.7% of homes. A seller with acreage can ask the PVA in Room 15 for the parcel record and compare it with a recent local sale before assuming the figure is right.

sections.h2: When are Bourbon County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office collects from November 1 through April 15. Paying sooner costs less, and the sheriff honors a U.S. postmark as the payment date.

Delinquent notices are mailed February 1. When April 15 ends, every unpaid bill leaves the sheriff's hands for the County Clerk, and the sheriff warns that significant extra fees follow. A spring seller should find out whether the bill has already moved.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Bourbon County tax bill?
sections.html:
Pay at the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or mail a check to that address. Bills are mailed to the homeowner as postcards, so a seller whose mortgage company pays from escrow should ask the lender whether it needs a copy.

  • Accepted: cash, cashier's checks, money orders, and personal or business checks drawn on U.S. banks.
  • Cards are taken in person only, with a 3.5% fee. The sheriff's own example is $55.13 on a $1,575 bill.
  • Third party checks and foreign funds are refused.
  • A returned check carries a $50 fee, and a bill paid with a bad check counts as unpaid.

sections.h2: Can I dispute a Bourbon County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes. Values are set as of January 1, and the first move is a conference with the PVA or a deputy, which comes before any paperwork.

KRS 133.120 governs the steps. Request the conference while the May inspection window is open, which is a two-week stretch that the state can lengthen for a county. If the PVA does not move your number, put your reasons and your own value estimate in a letter to the County Clerk, who passes it to the board of assessment appeals. The deadline is one workday after the window closes. At the hearing, bring evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal or a contractor's repair quote.

Filing never stops the bill. You pay on the value you claim, and if the board lands higher, the gap comes back with interest. Skipping the county board closes the door on the state-level Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Bourbon County?
sections.html:
Yes, the statewide one. Owners who reach age 65, or who are classed as totally disabled, can claim it. The Department of Revenue sets the deduction at $49,100 for the two years covering 2025 and 2026.

Applications go to the PVA in Room 15. The state's worked example: a $200,000 home is taxed as if it were worth $150,900. Disability claims repeat yearly, with exceptions for service-connected veterans and for owners the Social Security Administration or Kentucky Retirement Systems has ruled permanently disabled. The amount resets every other year, so ask the PVA for the figure that applies to your bill.

sections.h2: What does a late Bourbon County tax bill cost in real dollars?
sections.html:
Take a bill of $2,000. Paid during November it is $1,960 after the 2% discount. In December it is $2,000. In January the 5% penalty makes it $2,100, and from February 1 through April 15 the 21% period brings it to $2,420. That is a $460 spread between paying in November and waiting until the last collection day.

The sheriff posts that last stretch as a 21% penalty period, and the 21% is the figure used above. After April 15 the County Clerk adds its own fees, and the amount you owe is whatever the clerk quotes on the day you pay. Sellers with an unpaid bill from a past year should call the clerk for that number before setting a closing date.

sections.h2: What do other Bourbon County figures show about the housing market?
sections.html:
The county issued 109 building permits in 2025, far more than Boyd County's 12, and retail sales per person in 2022 were $39,822. Median household income was $61,354 for 2020 to 2024, and 13.9% of residents were in poverty. Some 94.9% of residents had stayed in the same house for a year, which points to a settled county where homes change hands slowly.

That steadiness helps a seller who has the paperwork in order. A buyer's lender or title company will want the current tax bill, the deed and any lien releases on the table at closing, and each of those comes from an office within one building at 301 Main Street.

sections.h2: What becomes of the tax bill when a Bourbon County house sells?
sections.html:
State law makes each year's tax a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and a lien rides with the house once a bill goes delinquent. The closing agent will confirm the bill is current.

  • Check with the sheriff on whether this year's bill is paid and in which collection period.
  • Give the buyer's mailing address in the deed's tax-bill line so the next postcard finds them.
  • Settle at closing how the year's tax is divided between you and the buyer.
  • For a past-due year, expect the clerk, not the sheriff, to quote the payoff.

Typical owner costs run $1,424 a month with a mortgage and $466 without one, so the tax bill is one piece of a larger monthly picture.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to avoid a penalty on a Bourbon County bill?
faqs.a: December 31 is the last day for the plain face amount. The 2% discount ends November 30, and the 5% penalty begins January 1.

faqs.q: Where can I hand over a Bourbon County tax payment?
faqs.a: At the Sheriff's Office, 301 Main Street, Suite 104, Paris, or by mail to that address. Card payments are accepted only in person, with a 3.5% fee.

faqs.q: What happens to a Bourbon County bill unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: The sheriff passes it to the County Clerk, and the sheriff's page says significant added fees apply.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Bourbon County property assessment?
faqs.a: Begin with a PVA conference in May. If it fails, send the County Clerk a written petition the workday after the inspection window closes.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for the Bourbon County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners aged 65 and up, plus owners classed as totally disabled, who file with the PVA. The state's deduction is $49,100 across 2025 and 2026.
